metaDescription: Six cabinet door organizers compared on mounting method, tier count, and fit, so you can use the unused back of a door without drilling or guessing.
introParagraphs: The back of a cabinet or pantry door is the most wasted storage in many kitchens, and the six organizers in this guide put it to work in two different ways. Over-the-door pantry racks like the Delamu, Moforoco, and POKIPO hang from the top of the door, while inside-cabinet racks such as the ORDORA, Sinnsally, and Sevenblue attach to the cabinet door itself.

The specs vary a lot. The Delamu is a six-basket rack measuring 18 inches wide and 50 inches tall, the Moforoco stacks nine tiers, and the POKIPO offers eight baskets with adjustable height. On the cabinet side, the ORDORA is a two-pack of six-tier lid racks with adhesive hooks listed at up to 22 pounds, and the Sevenblue offers adhesive or screw installation.
We evaluated these from product specs and buyer feedback, weighing clearance, mounting method, load, and ease of use.

products.name: Delamu 6-Tier Over the Door Pantry Organizer

specList.label: Overall size
specList.value: 18 in W x 50 in H x 5 in D

products.description:
The Delamu earns the top spot partly because its listing is honest about what has to be true for it to work. It spells out the overall size of 18 by 50 by 5 inches and tells you the pantry needs more than 5.2 inches of depth and a door gap above 0.06 inches. Six large baskets, each about 16.22 by 4.65 by 2.95 inches, hold boxes, cans, and bottles.

The listing gives a capacity of up to 60 pounds, a useful figure for heavy canned goods. The tradeoff is that over-the-door racks need clearance, and a door that sits tight in its frame may not close. It sits at a mid-range price tier, which is fair for a full-size rack.

Assembly is a simple snap together, so setup takes minutes. Hang it over the door, check that the door closes, and load heavy items at the bottom. Compared with the Moforoco, the Delamu has fewer tiers but deeper baskets.
products.bestFor: Pantry doors with enough clearance that need a sturdy, well-documented six-basket rack
pros: Six deep baskets for cans and boxes
Listed capacity of up to 60 lb

products.name: Sevenblue 2-Pack Metal Cabinet Door Organizer
products.description:
Sevenblue sells two metal organizers that mount on the inside of a cabinet door or on a wall. You can choose adhesive for a no-drill setup or screws for a firmer hold, which gives you control over how permanent the install is. They are meant for tumbler lids, container lids, bottles, and small kitchen tools.

Because they sit inside the door, they add thickness that can stop a door from closing if space is tight. The listing offers fewer capacity details than the Delamu, so keep loads light. At the lowest price tier here, they are the cheapest way to begin.

Check the space behind the door before mounting, then clean the surface for adhesive. Screws are the safer choice for heavier items. Compared with the Sinnsally, these are metal rather than clear plastic.
products.bestFor: Inside a cabinet door where you want a metal rack with a choice of mounting
pros: Two metal organizers in a pack
Lowest price tier in this group

products.name: ORDORA 2 Pack 6-Tier Pot Lid Rack for Cabinet Door
products.description:
ORDORA's racks do one job well: they store pot lids vertically on a cabinet door or wall. The U-shaped slot grips round, ear-knob, and other handle shapes, so lids stay put. Six tiers per rack give you room for a full set of lids.

Industrial-strength adhesive hooks are listed at up to 22 pounds, and they mount without damage. The tradeoff is that the racks are only useful for lids and flat items, and they add thickness behind the door. The low-to-mid price tier makes the pair a fair buy.

Stick them to a clean, dry surface and test the hold before loading. Mount at a comfortable reach height. Compared with the Sevenblue, the ORDORA is specialized for lids.
products.bestFor: Pot lids that need a vertical home on a cabinet door or wall
pros: Two racks of six tiers each
Adhesive hooks listed up to 22 lb
cons: Specialized for lids and flat items

products.name: POKIPO 8 Tier Over the Door Pantry Organizer
products.description:
POKIPO's rack has eight baskets whose height can be adjusted, which lets you fit tall bottles in some slots and short spice jars in others. The listing says it can hang over the door or mount on a wall, which adds flexibility if a door lacks clearance. A thicker, rust-resistant frame with water-resistant coating suggests it is built for a busy pantry.

The flexibility has a cost, because eight baskets is a taller, heavier unit. It sits at the highest price tier in this group. Baskets are also shallower than the Delamu's, so large boxes may not fit.

Set the heights before loading and check door clearance. Wall mounting needs a screwdriver. Compared with the Delamu, this offers more baskets and adjustable heights but less documentation on clearance.
products.bestFor: Pantries with mixed item sizes that benefit from adjustable basket heights
pros: Hangs over a door or mounts on a wall
cons: Highest price tier in this group

products.name: Moforoco White 9-Tier Over the Door Pantry Organizer
products.description:
The Moforoco stacks nine tiers, which makes it the highest-capacity rack in this guide. It is made of metal described as strong enough for heavy cans and jars, and it installs over any standard door with no tools or drilling. That convenience is a big plus for renters.

Nine tiers make the unit tall and the shelves shallow, so large boxes will not fit. It also adds weight to the door, which may strain hinges on lightweight doors. It sits at an upper price tier, a bit below the POKIPO.

Hang it, check that the door closes, and load heavy items on the lower tiers. Wipe the white finish with a damp cloth. Compared with the Delamu, you get more tiers but shallower baskets.
products.bestFor: Small items and spices in a tall rack that needs maximum tier count without drilling
pros: Nine tiers for the highest capacity here
Metal built for heavy cans and jars
cons: Shallow tiers do not fit large boxes

products.name: Sinnsally 2 Pack Cabinet Door Organizer
products.description:
Sinnsally's boxes are clear PET plastic with adhesive strips, so they stick to a cabinet door with no drilling. They store food container lids, tumbler lids, and similar items, and the transparent walls make it easy to see what is inside. Two boxes in a pack cover two doors or one big one.

The tradeoff is hold strength, since adhesive strips suit light items. PET is shatter-resistant but not as sturdy as metal. At a low price tier, they are an inexpensive entry.

Clean the door first, press the strip, and wait before loading. Wipe the clear boxes with a damp cloth. Compared with the Sevenblue, these are see-through but less rigid.
products.bestFor: Light lids and small items where clear storage and no-drill mounting matter
pros: Two clear boxes in a pack

buyingCriteria.explanation: An organizer is useless if the door will not close. The Delamu states a pantry depth over 5.2 inches and a door gap above 0.06 inches, while inside-cabinet racks like the Sevenblue and Sinnsally add thickness behind the door. Measure the gap at the hinge and latch sides. Leave room for contents to clear the shelf.

Over-the-door racks hook on with no tools, as with the Moforoco, while adhesive racks like the Sinnsally need a clean surface. The Sevenblue offers adhesive or screws, and the POKIPO can mount to a wall. Screws hold best for heavy items. Renters should check what can be removed cleanly.

The Delamu lists up to 60 pounds, and the ORDORA's adhesive hooks list up to 22 pounds. The others give limited figures. Sellers' capacity numbers are claims, not independent tests. Keep loads well below the listed limit.

More tiers mean shallower shelves. The Moforoco has nine tiers and the POKIPO eight, while the Delamu has six deep baskets about 16 inches wide. Check the largest item you store. Choose fewer tiers for boxes and more for spice jars.
A loaded rack adds weight to the door, which may strain hinges. Tall racks like the Moforoco and POKIPO add more. Check that the door still swings freely. Load heavy items at the bottom.

Door storage keeps items at hand height instead of low on a shelf. Racks like the Delamu put cans within easy reach, and inside-door racks like the ORDORA keep lids visible. Place daily items at waist to shoulder height. Avoid putting heavy items on the top tier.

howWeEvaluated.title: Door fit and clearance
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how clearly each listing explains clearance, from the Delamu's stated depth and gap to the others' general fit claims. Clear guidance earns credit. This was the heaviest factor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mounting and install
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each rack attaches and how removable it is. The Moforoco needs no tools, and the Sevenblue offers adhesive or screws. Easier install earns credit if hold strength stays adequate.

howWeEvaluated.title: Load capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the stated capacity and hook strength, such as the Delamu's 60 pound figure and the ORDORA's 22 pound hooks. Picks without a stated figure were treated cautiously. The strongest pick leads here, and the most basic, the Sinnsally, trails.

howWeEvaluated.title: Layout and access
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tier counts, basket depths, and visibility. The Delamu's deep baskets and the Moforoco's nine tiers serve different needs. Layouts that match real items score higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for price tier
howWeEvaluated.description: Higher tiers must add capacity or adjustability. We favored honest specs.

rows: Six deep baskets with stated clearance
Tall pantry door, many small items

howToChoose.subheading: Over the Door vs Inside the Cabinet
howToChoose.intro: The location of the rack changes what it can hold.

cards.label: Over the door
cards.text: The Delamu, Moforoco, and POKIPO hang over a pantry door and hold cans and boxes. They need depth and a door gap. Pick this side for pantry storage.

cards.label: Inside the cabinet
cards.text: The ORDORA, Sinnsally, and Sevenblue stick or screw to the inside of a door and hold lids and small items. They add thickness. Pick this side for lids and tools.

howToChoose.note: In short, pick the Delamu for a pantry and the ORDORA for lids.

howToChoose.subheading: For Pantry Cans and Boxes Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for deep baskets, a stated weight rating, and enough pantry depth. Measure the door gap first.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Delamu's listed 60 pound capacity and deep baskets fit this best, while the Moforoco suits small cans and spice jars.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need adjustable heights or maximum tiers. The POKIPO and Moforoco justify higher tiers.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only store lids or light items. The Sevenblue, Sinnsally, and ORDORA cover that at lower tiers.

faq.q: How do I choose between the Delamu and the Moforoco?
faq.a: The Delamu has six deep baskets and lists up to 60 pounds. The Moforoco has nine shallower tiers and needs no tools. Choose the Delamu for cans and boxes and the Moforoco for small items.

faq.q: What is the cheapest cabinet door organizer here?
faq.a: The Sevenblue and Sinnsally sit at the lowest tiers. Both suit light items. The ORDORA is the next step up.
Check the gap first. The Delamu states a pantry depth over 5.2 inches and a door gap above 0.06 inches. Inside-door racks add thickness, so measure the shelf behind the door.

faq.q: Can I install these without drilling?
faq.a: Yes, the Moforoco hangs on with no tools, and the Sinnsally and ORDORA use adhesive. The Sevenblue lets you choose adhesive or screws. Clean the surface well for adhesive.
The ORDORA lists up to 22 pounds for its adhesive hooks. Adhesive works best on clean, flat surfaces. Use screws for heavy loads.
Over-the-door racks hang on without damage, and adhesive types are described as non-perforating. Screws leave holes. Check the finish before removing adhesive.
